output.brief: The overtime overrun comes mainly from the closing contract ending, not from the hiring freeze. Call-back pay rose from $38k to $289k. 1,962 of the 2,295 call-backs carry the CLOSE task code, and all are dated 1 April or later. None are in Summit Hill, whose closing contract continued. The three districts that lost the contract account for nearly all the increase. Summit Hill has 5 vacancies and its overtime was nearly flat. Eastgate has only 1 vacancy and its overtime nearly doubled. Holdover overtime grew only 1.5% in hours, so vacancies and heat explain little. The vacancy-versus-overtime correlation is mostly a coincidence of timing. Both rose in April. Internal Audit checked the fraud allegation against lock logs and found no padding, so don't discipline R-14 and R-22. Each 30–45 minute closing round is paid as three hours under the call-back minimum. That makes in-house closing far more costly than the $96k contract. I'm fairly confident, and I'd restore contracted closing now and track call-back spending. Don't impose an overtime cap, because members say they would stop taking call-backs and the sites wouldn't get locked. Keep the Eastgate favoritism concern open: sign-up sheets are being thrown away, so keep them from now on and review the assignment pattern before acting on the supervisor. The injury link to overtime is unproven, because claims aren't matched to hours worked. Match them to payroll. Don't pursue the eleven-position exemption as the fix.
